evidence: Plan: "`docs/architecture.md` mentions \"the transport retry policy (ADR 0037)\". The 0037 group ... moves `0037-transport-retry` -> **0087**"
search_files 'ADR 0037' in docs/architecture.md -> (no matches); search 'retry' in docs/architecture.md -> (no matches)
Actual reference: docs/config.md:306 '[ADR 0037](adr/0037-transport-retry.md)'
findings.finding: The 'Worked example' asserts that `docs/architecture.md` mentions "the transport retry policy (ADR 0037)", but architecture.md contains no 'ADR 0037' reference (nor even the word 'retry'). The real adr/0037-transport-retry reference is at `docs/config.md:306`.
scenarios: Implementer follows the worked example to build/verify the sweep, edits or greps architecture.md, finds nothing, and mistrusts or mis-scopes the resolution table

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define where the 'workstream' grouping key comes from (an ADR front-matter field, a filename-prefix convention, or an explicit mapping) so the generated README grouping is deterministic.
evidence: Header: '83 files ... all flat in one directory'
'grouped by workstream' with no stated source for the workstream attribute per ADR
findings.finding: The README index AC requires grouping 'by workstream', but ADRs are described as flat files in one directory with no stated workstream metadata; the source/derivation of the workstream grouping key is undefined.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'A generated docs/adr/README.md index exists, grouped by workstream, showing full slugs'

findings.finding: AC3 requires the generated README index be 'grouped by workstream, showing full slugs', but 'workstream' is never defined — there is no stated mapping from an ADR to its workstream, nor a rule for deriving it (from a header field, directory, filename prefix, or the RENUMBERING tiers).
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the grouping source, e.g. 'group by a Workstream: header added to each ADR; ADRs lacking one are grouped under Uncategorized', and note where that field comes from.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:64 find_broken_links() walks docs_dir.rglob('*.md') and reports every relative markdown link (']( target )') that does not resolve within docs/ — this covers docs/adr/*.md bodies and links like adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md
.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:468-477 already runs 'python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check' as the 'Docs-index completeness gate', failing the build on any broken docs-internal link

All ADR references found in docs/ are markdown-link form, e.g. docs/architecture.md:204 '[ADR 0055](adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md)', docs/config.md:306 '[ADR 0037](adr/0037-transport-retry.md)' — exactly the target class find_broken_links already validates
tests/unit/test_check_docs_index.py:195 test_all_docs_relative_links_resolve additionally asserts every relative link in docs/ resolves
The plan does not mention check_docs_index.py or state how the new check relates to it
findings.finding: The addendum's proposed scripts/check_adr_numbers.py referential-integrity assertion (fail when an adr/NNNN-slug link in docs/ points to a non-existent filename) rebuilds functionality already provided and CI-enforced by scripts/check_docs_index.py.
findings.location: Section 'Cross-reference handling', 'Proving command (new AC below)' + AC addendum line

Future maintenance: two scripts with divergent link-parsing regexes disagree on what counts as a broken docs link
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Proving command' paragraph and the addendum AC, note that broken adr/*-slug.md markdown links are already caught by scripts/check_docs_index.py --check (wired at _build-and-test.yml 'Docs-index completeness gate'); limit check_adr_numbers.py to the marker bijection/uniqueness and the number-to-final-file rewrite verification, delegating raw dead-link detection to the existing gate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the per-number marker-file conflict mechanism against the established ADR-ecosystem alternative of dropping the monotonic sequential counter for a naturally collision-free identifier (date-prefix / ULID / UUIDv7 / content-hash), stating explicitly why the sequential number and its coordination machinery are retained.
evidence: Plan quote: 'The race-free mechanism is a per-number marker file docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN whose content is the ADR's filename: two ADRs claiming one number produce an add/add conflict'
Plan considers only 'A shared sorted index was tested and rejected' and 'A pre-merge uniqueness check on a monotonic counter is racy' — both keep the sequential counter

Retrieved prior art: ULID spec (github.com/ulid/spec) targets 'unique IDs without centralized allocation' with lexicographic time-sort; a real ADR (github.com/jakobwesthoff/ntropy docs/adr/0004) documents adopting a sortable ID for 'identifier strategy: sortable IDs without centralized allocation' to avoid centralized-number collisions
ABSENCE: the plan states collisions arise from a monotonic counter but never evaluates removing that counter, so the root-cause remedy used elsewhere in the ADR ecosystem is unconsidered
findings.finding: The plan justifies its novel marker-file conflict-forcing mechanism only against two same-family alternatives (racy CI check; spurious-conflict sorted index) and never weighs the established ADR-community approach that eliminates the collision class at its root: replacing the central monotonic sequential number with a naturally collision-free identifier (date-prefix, ULID/UUIDv7 time-sortable ID, or content-hash).
findings.location: Design section: 'Prevention is git's, not CI's.' and Acceptance Criteria (marker files + bijection check)
scenarios: Reviewers/adopters ask why the repo adds a marker-file coordination layer and CI bijection check instead of switching new ADRs to a collision-free ID scheme that needs no conflict detection
Future ADR additions still require the .numbers/ marker discipline and CI enforcement indefinitely, whereas a non-sequential ID would make new collisions structurally impossible

findings.finding: Renumbering moves 22 ADRs to new numbers; any existing doc, ADR cross-reference, or commit trailer that cites a moved ADR by its OLD number becomes stale. The plan handles historical COMMIT references (RENUMBERING resolution table) and gerrit-aws-setup.md:602, but does not require sweeping the tree (other ADRs, AGENTS.md, docs) for now-stale references to the 22 moved numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'CI or a one-time sweep confirms no non-historical reference in docs/ or ADR bodies cites a moved ADR by its pre-renumbering number.'

findings.finding: The renumbering moves ADRs from 17 duplicate numbers, but only three consumer files (AGENTS.md:42, CONTRIBUTING.md:173, docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:602) are named for update. Many bare-number ADR references to soon-moved numbers live OUTSIDE docs/adr/ and are unenumerated: ADR 0037 (a 5-way collision) is cited in rebar.toml:32, src/rebar/_config_schema.py:224, src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py:12, scripts/run_live_matrix.py:2, tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py:461, tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:14, tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py (several), tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py:323, docs/reuse-surface.md:431, docs/config.md:306, docs/review-kernel.md:113; ADR-0010 (doubled) in infra/terraform/monitoring_s5.tf:37,56, infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md:10; ADR 0007 (3x) in CHANGELOG.md:618. When these numbers' movers are renumbered, these bare references become wrong or ambiguous.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (renumbering / reference-resolution ACs); plan omits non-doc consumers
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC to sweep the whole repo for bare `ADR NNNN`/`ADR-NNNN` references to any renumbered number and update them to the new number (or the kept number where the reference is unambiguously the earliest-landed ADR), and record each in RENUMBERING.md's resolution table alongside the historical-commit rows.

findings.finding: The CURRENT-STATE CORRECTION's claim of '74 distinct numbers' is refuted by the tree: 91 files with 22 movers yields 69 distinct numbers, and the ADR corpus contains exactly the contiguous numbers 0001–0069 (69 distinct), with none above 0069.
findings.location: CURRENT-STATE CORRECTION, first bullet ('91 ADR files, 74 distinct numbers, 17 duplicate numbers')
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '74 distinct numbers' with '69 distinct numbers' in the first bullet of the CURRENT-STATE CORRECTION.

findings.checklist_item: Extend the referential-integrity check (or the sweep + UNRESOLVED accounting) to cover path-form bare-number references such as `docs/adr/NNNN` (no slug) in docs/ and src/, since these are not prose and can point at collision numbers (e.g. src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:230 `docs/adr/0015`).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:230: 'See docs/adr/0015 + 0017 + docs/plan-review-gate.md.'
0015 is a collision number (0015-code-review-voter-four-pass-rewire.md and 0015-project-supplied-criteria.md)
Plan: check 'fails when any adr/NNNN-slug link in docs/ points to a filename that does not exist, or any docs/adr/*.md body cross-links a slug/number with no matching file'
Plan carve-out: 'Bare prose "ADR NNNN" with no slug is advisory-only ... recorded UNRESOLVED' — but `docs/adr/0015` is a path form in src/, not prose, and won't be flagged
findings.finding: The referential-integrity check's coverage has a gap: path-form bare-number references like `docs/adr/0015` (no slug) at a collision number are neither caught by the `adr/NNNN-slug` link clause nor the `docs/adr/*.md` body cross-link clause, yet they are real path references (not advisory prose) that will silently strand.
findings.location: Cross-reference handling / Acceptance Criteria (addendum) proving-command scope
scenarios: A source-code path reference `docs/adr/0015` remains pointing at a collision number after renumbering; the check passes but the reference is ambiguous/stranded
findings.suggested_fix: Have scripts/check_adr_numbers.py match the `docs/adr/NNNN` path prefix even without a `-slug` suffix; when NNNN is (or was) a collision number, require it to be resolved to a specific final-numbered slug during the sweep, or explicitly record it UNRESOLVED in RENUMBERING.md rather than treating only slugless prose as advisory.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CI assertion that the committed docs/adr/README.md byte-matches a fresh regeneration (fail non-zero on drift), so the index cannot silently go stale.
evidence: AC states the index 'exists' but the CI-asserted checks enumerated are bijection, no-shared-content, and referential integrity — not index freshness
ABSENCE: no proving command that regenerate == committed README
findings.finding: The README index is described as 'generated' but no acceptance criterion or CI check asserts the committed README matches a fresh regeneration, so it can silently drift out of sync after future ADR additions.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'A generated docs/adr/README.md index exists' and the CI check scripts/check_adr_numbers.py
scenarios: A new ADR lands, marker+file added, but README not regenerated; CI stays green while index is stale
findings.suggested_fix: Have scripts/check_adr_numbers.py (or a sibling) regenerate the index to a temp file and diff against the committed README, exiting non-zero on mismatch.
